text.p: Talisman Energy Inc called into question on Wednesday a new oil and gas reserve tally released by takeover target Wascana Energy Inc.
"We're surprised by the magnitude of the reserve change," Talisman spokesman Dave Mann said.
"It makes you wonder either how could the numbers have been so incorrect before, or how have they grown so dramatically in the last three weeks?"

Earlier this week, Wascana released data from a recent reserve evaluation completed by Ryder Scott Co that revealed oil and gas reserves that were dramatically higher than had been detailed in its 1996 financial results.

Wascana, which has rejected Talisman's C$1.7 billion offer in an increasingly bitter war of words, said its proven reserves climbed to 236 million barrels of oil equivalent, a 29 percent jump over previously released numbers.
Proven plus probable reserves were 24 percent higher at 303 million BOE, Wascana said.
It also this week projected 1998 production and cash flow figures that were well above most analyst estimates.

"We haven't seen what Ryder Scott have done, don't know if this is done on spec, done predominantly using 3-D seismic or really what is going on here," Mann said. "The numbers sound suspicious, but it's difficult to comment until we see how it's done."

Mann said Talisman was also surprised by Wascana's contention that its shareholders would contribute 24 percent of the economic value to the merged entity, but only receive 16 percent of the common shares.
"If you do the math correctly and you factor in the C$615 million in cash and magically it takes you back to 24-25 percent," he said.
Talisman has offered C$18.50 cash or 0.41 of a Talisman share for each Wascana share.

Mann said he did not know if Wascana's board had replied yet to Talisman's requests for a meeting with the target's special bid committee and access to its confidential financial and operating data room.
Data room access would allow Talisman to better judge the merits of the Wascana reserves information and financial and operating projections, he said.
